threatFindings.threat: A byte-level change of the anchor/dwell encoding that is safe against both MOVSB and MOVSW trails exists
threatFindings.evidence: Static residue analysis: MOVSB trails write 4-byte blocks starting at residue 2, MOVSW at residue 3. Any 2-byte dwell instruction is either split by one family (transient opcode with the foreign byte) or overwritten atomically with foreign non-trigger bytes (e.g. FB 0F from V6-family CS words, 0F invalid in Cpu.java). Agrees with B051/B061.

threatFindings.threat: Lattice offset choice changes how often MOVSW trails cover our anchor
threatFindings.evidence: Static page count: a 300h MOVSW trail covers our in-page offset on 3 pages per generation whatever our offset; our 400h trail covers theirs on 4 pages. Only timing decides who is crossed first.
